slides.title: More Channels Means More Risk to Manage
bullets: Digital activity multiplies touchpoints with the scientific community
It also multiplies regulatory, legal and reputational risk
Same discipline as in-person activity applies, or more
Compliance enables sustainable digital growth, not blocks it

slides.title: MLR Review Applies to Every Digital Piece
bullets: Same MLR review as print material or visit presentations
Digital demands faster, more scalable review processes
Volume and speed of content push adoption of dedicated platforms
Rigor stays intact even as review gets more efficient

slides.title: Transparency in Every DOL Collaboration
bullets: Same disclosure standards as any traditional KOL relationship
Conflicts of interest must be disclosed clearly
Scientific support must stay separate from promotional activity
Compliance teams should partner with DOLs, not just police them

slides.title: Traceability That Survives an Audit
bullets: Shared content and third-party interactions must be recorded
Medical listening findings used in decisions need documentation
Must hold up under internal audit or regulatory inspection
Connects to broader industry transparency obligations

slides.title: Compliance Lives in Every Personal Interaction
bullets: Not the exclusive job of a specialized team
A LinkedIn comment carries the same standard as a field visit
Same rigor, affiliation transparency, and non-promotional separation
Adapted to a public, permanent, faster environment

takeaway.title: Digital compliance is what makes sustainable digital scientific engagement possible
bullets: MLR review, DOL transparency and traceability are the three pillars
DOL collaborations need the same disclosure standards as traditional KOLs
Every MSL digital interaction carries the same compliance standard as the field
